column1: # REQ-036 mechanism check: per-type curvature spread @ step 2250 = std of log10(top_eigenvalue) across the 6 matrix types. Smaller = more equalized curvature. (Checkpoint at 2250 per the cadence note; equilibrium stable.)
# KEY FINDING: the intervention does exactly what it targets -- a5 polar equalizes per-type curvature the MOST (0.128 vs control 0.246),
# a4 anti-rule ANTI-equalizes (0.444). But equalization is INVERSELY related to val quality: the arm that equalized curvature most (a5)
# has the WORST val@2750; control (least equalized) has the BEST. So per-type LR successfully equalizes equilibrium curvature (mechanism real),
# but the premise "equal per-type equilibrium curvature is better" is FALSIFIED -- equalizing it HURTS training loss at this fork/horizon.
